scope: secret-free read-only production observation plus isolated exact-snapshot restore equality

dirtyData.observationDelta: Compared with the v3 source refresh, 50 jobs were added: 46 SENT, 3 PENDING and 1 SENDING; stale SENDING increased from 11 to 14. No row identifier or payload was emitted and no row was mutated.

failClosedRehearsalNotes: The host TCP read-only DSN path failed closed before any snapshot; the source observation used a local container-socket read-only PostgreSQL session instead, without printing credentials.

The source session set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=0 only for that bounded read-only transaction so the exported snapshot remained open during pg_dump; no server setting or production row changed.

The final restore used tracked bootstrap_roles.sql, prepare_database.sql, pg_restore --role=obsidian_migrator --no-owner --no-privileges and runtime_privileges.sql; an earlier ad-hoc normalization was excluded from final evidence.
The custom archive passed pg_restore --list. The archive, digest-only manifests, disposable containers and tmpfs were removed after equality checks.
claimBoundary: The production source transaction and pg_dump were read-only and bound to one exported MVCC snapshot.
Table equality is a 54-table row-multiset projection; catalog equality covers only the 13 declared v2 sections.

Owners, ACLs and selected cluster globals were deterministically reconstructed through the tracked bootstrap/prepare/role-bound restore/runtime privilege sequence; the archive itself carried no owner or privilege statements.
Sequence runtime state, physical backup, PITR and complete PostgreSQL catalog equality are not claimed.
Fresh evidence cannot authorize acceptance, 064B, row disposition, deployment, restart, cutover or Telegram delivery.
